beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:respectful, measured storytelling][tune:fall]The Mahabharata, one of India's great sacred epics, says the sea rushed into Krishna's ^golden city of Dwarka, and ^swallowed it.

[d:tension][act:intrigued, reporting][tune:fall]Today, off the coast of Gujarat, in western India, divers have found stone ^blocks on the sea floor. [act:adding the surprise, brighter][tune:fall]And more than a hundred ^anchors.

[d:calm][act:crediting the work, steady][tune:fall]India's oceanographers dived off the modern town of Dwarka for ^years. [act:listing, steady][tune:level]They mapped dressed blocks, curved walls and anchors, three to ^sixteen metres down. [go:1|0][act:adding, quietly impressed][tune:fall]And on the nearby island of Bet Dwarka, they found a ^settlement about thirty-five ^hundred years old.

[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:intrigue, building][tune:fall]Then, in {2001|two thousand one}, a sonar survey@noun in the Gulf of Khambhat, further east, showed ^geometric shapes, ^forty metres down. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Sonar works like shouting into a canyon: it sends sound down, listens for the ^echo, and paints a picture of the ^floor. [go:3|0][act:careful, precise][tune:fall]A dredged piece of wood from there was dated to about {7500|seventy-five hundred} BCE.
[d:tension][act:awed, then careful][tune:fall]That would be older than ^any city on Earth. [gap:0.4][act:the caveat, quiet][tune:fallrise]^If it's a city.

[d:build][act:plain, careful][tune:fall]But ^nothing at Khambhat was ^excavated. [act:matter of fact][tune:fall]Everything was dredged up ^blind, with ^no layers. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Layers are like the pages of a book: they tell you what lay with what, and in what order. [act:explaining, a simple picture]A dredge rips out the pages and shuffles them. [act:simple logic, gentle][tune:fall]And a date on wood dates the ^wood: when the tree died, not who used@verb it, or when.

[d:build][act:explaining, clear][tune:fall]Off Dwarka, the anchors are the kinds ^traders used@verb from about two thousand years ago into ^medieval times. [act:vivid, a little wistful][tune:fall]A busy ^harbour, ^eaten by the sea.

[d:reveal][act:respectful, the real story][tune:fall]So the sea ^did swallow a Dwarka: a harbour, slowly, over ^centuries. [sfx:hit][act:news, brightening][tune:fall]And in {2025|twenty twenty-five}, India's archaeological survey@noun went back ^underwater, to look again. [act:open, suspenseful][tune:fall]The results aren't out ^yet.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, respectful and calm][tune:rise]A city from the age of the ^epic, under the sea? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Awaiting ^evidence*. [act:plain, simple][tune:rise]A ^drowned harbour? [act:firm, simple][tune:highfall]^Real. [p:0.93][act:with respect, sincere][tune:fall]What Dwarka means to the faithful is not ours to weigh: only the ^stones, the ^dates and the ^sediments.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, hopeful][tune:fall]The ^next dive report could ^change this card.
